advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Wrap the `reset --hard` adoption (lines 130-132) in an `else:` so the two lock-held-precondition `warn` branches (lines 123-126) actually skip the destructive reset.
evidence: infra/scripts/reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh:124:                    warn(current_problem or pinned_problem or "unreadable store epoch")
infra/scripts/reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh:125:                elif current_epoch is not None or not isinstance(pinned_epoch, str):
infra/scripts/reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh:126:                    warn("epoch adoption preconditions changed while waiting for the write lock")

The comment at line 111 states 'Re-check every destructive precondition while holding rebar's unified write lock' — but the re-check result never gates the reset; the reset is unconditional after the warns.
advisory.finding: In the epoch-adoption heredoc, the lock-held re-check warns on failed preconditions (unreadable epoch, or preconditions changed while waiting for the lock) but does NOT skip the destructive `git reset --hard`: lines 130-132 sit at the same indentation as the `if`/`elif` at lines 123-126, not inside an `else`. So after warning, the code still resets the clone to the pinned remote, discarding local state — the exact destructive action the re-check exists to prevent.
scenarios: A concurrent writer advances local HEAD's epoch (current_epoch becomes non-None) or corrupts/updates the record while the ensure script waits for the write lock: the guard warns then still `reset --hard`s, destroying the newly-written local state.
The remote record becomes unreadable between fetch and lock acquisition (pinned_problem set): warns then resets anyway.
advisory.suggested_fix: Make lines 127-138 the `else:` of the `if current_problem or pinned_problem / elif current_epoch is not None ...` chain (add `else:` and indent the adoption block one level), so a failed lock-held re-check returns without resetting.

advisory.finding: The under-lock precondition-recheck block added to reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh (the 'local HEAD changed while waiting', 'working tree has uncommitted changes', and 'epoch adoption preconditions changed' guards, lines 111-138) has no test. Every convergence-matrix and happy-path scenario is decided by the PRE-lock checks; none forces a state that passes the pre-lock gate but changes/fails under the write lock. In particular the dirty-worktree guard (line 118) is never exercised — all local-history cases commit via commit_local_file and never leave an uncommitted change. A regression in these destructive-operation safety guards (which the change explicitly introduces) would not be caught. This is aggravated by an apparent fall-through: lines 123-126 warn but do not skip the `git reset --hard` at line 131, so the 'preconditions changed' guard adopts anyway — and no test detects it.
